subject: core-gate-harness-specifications.v2
role: The revised authoring act for the five core gate harness identifiers, landing one finding of mine and three of Codex's against v1.
verdictRule: ACCEPT only at 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX. Measured: 0 blockers, 1 SHOULD-FIX. The rule is not discretionary, so the verdict is REJECT.
acceptanceGrade: REJECT-ON-ONE-MECHANISM. All four dispositions land and the unit repair is exactly right. The new Linux no-load mechanism conflicts with the D-102 protocol this artifact says it does not amend.

reviewerErrorsAtV1.disclosure: I rejected v1 on one finding, the G03 backticks. Codex found three more and was right on all three. They share one shape and I record it plainly.

byteConstants.what: v1 pinned 26214400 and 83886080 as the D-006 bounds in bytes.
byteConstants.howIMissedIt: Worse than missing it — I endorsed it. My v1 verdict recorded that '26214400 is exactly 25 MiB and 83886080 is exactly 80 MiB, so both byte figures the fixtures pin are correct rather than approximations.' I verified the multiplication and never asked whether the multiplier was decided. D-006 contains no MiB, no 1024, no 1048576 and no SI statement — I confirmed that this round by searching its full text — so 25 MB could as easily be 25,000,000 bytes, a 4.86% difference against a threshold governed by a 10% regression rule. Checking arithmetic is not checking the premise the arithmetic rests on.

vacuousMechanisms.what: v1's G03 asserted a trace 'proving no component or project load' with no observation mechanism, v1's G04 named RSS traces with no sampling protocol, and v1's G05 said deltas came 'with methodology' without stating one.
vacuousMechanisms.howIMissedIt: I applied the wrong lens. For the join artifacts the question is whether every claim traces to a recorded source, and I ran that check thoroughly here too — every threshold, machine and rank did trace. But this is an authoring artifact, and the question for authoring is whether a harness author could build from it. A specification that names a method instead of specifying one passes a citation audit and fails its own purpose.

reviewerErrorsAtV1.correctionApplied: This round I read D-102's measurement contract in full rather than accepting the artifact's 'does not amend that protocol', and asked of each new mechanism whether it is executable and whether it is consistent with what already governs. That is what produced the one finding below.

dispositionAudit.claimed: G03 claimVerbatim restored to live-cell backticks
dispositionAudit.verification: All five claimVerbatim values now compare byte-exact with == against their live claim cells, G03 included. All five owners are likewise byte-exact and all five harness identifiers occur in their own live harness cells.

dispositionAudit.claimed: invented 26214400/83886080 removed; d006UnitStanding UNDECIDED; OBL-2 not closed
dispositionAudit.verification: The only two seven-plus-digit numbers left in the file are 26214400 and 83886080, and all four occurrences are refusals — 'does not pin … as an authorized threshold' and 'read as authorizing … as the D-006 bound'. d006UnitStanding states the byte meaning is UNDECIDED because D-006 defines MB as neither 1e6 nor 2^20, which I confirmed independently against D-006's full text, and correctly notes that D-102's GiB definition is scoped to RAM matching — I checked that too, and D-102's GiB appears only in the RAM step of preflight. The closure list is now empty and OBL-2-UNIT-ACCOUNTING joins OD-101-1 and OD-101-2 as remaining leftover, so the artifact declines to close the obligation it was authored to close rather than claiming a closure the unit question will not support. That is the honest outcome.
dispositionAudit.noSubstituteConversionSmuggled: rssProtocol's 'VmRSS (kB) * 1024' is the /proc unit definition and matches D-102's own 'MemTotal kB × 1024', not a D-006 MB conversion. I checked this specifically because the dispatch forbids inventing one.

dispositionAudit.claimed: G03 noLoadProtocol and G04 rssProtocol added
dispositionAudit.verification: Both blocks exist and are substantive. noLoadProtocol supplies two digest-pinned hostile fixtures, an initial state that prevents accidental resolution, a load definition distinguishing an opened path from a merely present one, and a pass rule under which missing observation fails rather than passes — which is exactly the vacuity Codex charged. rssProtocol scopes sampling to T rather than the job VM, names a primitive per platform, a 10 ms window, and peak and steady derivations. The mechanism is no longer a label. What it is not is consistent with D-102 on Linux.

dispositionAudit.claimed: G05 pairedWorkload and delta formula added
dispositionAudit.verification: pairedWorkload defines both arms, a command that is neither analyze nor a consented probe, identical start endpoints on both sides, the RSS quantity, N=21 matched pairs for start and RSS with exact-byte publication for download and install, a median-difference delta formula, and a non-negative sign rule with the reason a negative delta is a failure. It also keeps D-006's no-cap disposition and adds fail conditions for using G03/G04 baselines or analyze as the workload.

shouldFix.title: The Linux no-load mechanism puts ptrace on a timing sample, which D-102 forbids in the same contract this artifact says it does not amend
shouldFix.finding: noLoadProtocol.eventStream reads 'Linux: strace -f -e trace=file,process of the timed child T from exec handshake to exit.' strace is ptrace-based. D-102's preflight paragraph reads 'Architecture observation is a dedicated launch of the same P+D. It is never a G03/G04 timing sample. After the fields below are recorded the preflight child is SIGKILLed and reaped. Timing samples of the same P+D then proceed without ptrace or suspend.' G03's exactByteIntent puts the latencies and the retained event stream in the same job record, and the mechanism names the timed child explicitly, so as written the traced launch is a timing sample. The artifact's own protocol field says 'This specification does not amend that protocol.'
shouldFix.whyItMatters: Executed as written the harness either violates D-102's no-ptrace rule for timing samples, or measures G03's latencies under strace and compares perturbed numbers to D-006's 100/150/250 ms cold bounds — bounds that are scored now, since milliseconds need no unit successor. Either outcome defeats the gate. The macOS branch does not have this problem: fs_usage is kdebug-based and the sandbox-profile alternative is a denial policy, so neither ptraces nor suspends.
shouldFix.whyNotBlocker: Nothing false is asserted about D-102, and a charitable author could read the no-load run as its own launch rather than the timing sample. The conflict is between a newly specified mechanism and an adopted contract, not a misstatement of that contract. I record that Codex may reasonably grade it a blocker, since following the text literally breaks a recorded decision.
shouldFix.repair: Follow the pattern D-102 already supplies for observation: specify the no-load evidence as a dedicated launch that is never a timing sample, SIGKILLed and reaped like preflight, or name a Linux mechanism that neither ptraces nor suspends the timed child. Either way state that the timed samples proceed clean, so the artifact's 'does not amend that protocol' holds on its face.

consideredAndDeclined.item: Charging the deferral of G01/G02/G04 bound comparisons as a weakening of the gates
consideredAndDeclined.whyDeclined: It is the honest consequence of the unit question, not a weakening. The artifact keeps every non-byte-denominated property scored now and says plainly that OBL-2 does not close on this limb. Pretending a bound is enforceable when its unit is undecided is the failure I committed at v1 by blessing an invented conversion.

consideredAndDeclined.item: Charging the macOS fs_usage branch alongside the Linux one
consideredAndDeclined.whyDeclined: fs_usage is kdebug-based and the sandbox-profile alternative is a denial policy; neither ptraces nor suspends the timed child, so neither collides with D-102's rule. Scoping the finding to the Linux branch is what the evidence supports.

rejectRule: ACCEPT only at 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX. One SHOULD-FIX is recorded, so the verdict is REJECT.
pathToAccept: Change the Linux no-load mechanism so the observed launch is not a timing sample, or name a mechanism that neither ptraces nor suspends. Nothing else needs to change: the unit standing, the three other repairs, every numeral, machine, owner, identifier and refusal survive as they stand.

What I know of the three Codex findings comes from the prompt's summaries plus my own re-derivation from D-006's and D-102's text, which is how I confirmed the byte-constant finding was right rather than taking it on trust — and that re-derivation is what showed my v1 endorsement of those constants was wrong.
independence.priorParticipation: I reviewed v1 and cleared three defects Codex caught. Both failure modes are disclosed above: endorsing arithmetic without checking its premise, and auditing citations in an artifact that needed auditing for executability.

coordinatorSummary: REJECT at 0 blockers and 1 SHOULD-FIX. Fifteen attacks run, one landed. Read the disclosure first: I rejected v1 on the G03 backticks alone and Codex found three more. The worst is that v1 pinned 26214400 and 83886080 as D-006's bounds and I did not merely miss it, I endorsed it — my v1 verdict called the figures 'exactly right'. D-006 contains no MiB, no 1024, no 1048576 and no SI statement, which I confirmed this round by searching its full text, so 25 MB may as well be 25,000,000 bytes, a 4.86% gap under a 10% regression rule. I checked the multiplication and never asked whether the multiplier was decided. The other two misses share a lens error: for join artifacts the question is whether every claim traces to a source, and I ran that check thoroughly here, but for an authoring artifact the question is whether a harness author could build from it, and v1 named methods where it needed to specify them. All four dispositions land. The five claimVerbatim and owner fields are now byte-exact, the byte constants survive only inside refusals, no substitute conversion is smuggled through rssProtocol's kB arithmetic — that is /proc's unit and D-102's own convention — and d006UnitStanding correctly records the meaning as UNDECIDED while noting D-102's GiB is scoped to RAM matching, which I verified. The honest consequence is that OBL-2 does not close: the closure list is empty and OBL-2-UNIT-ACCOUNTING joins the two open decisions as remaining leftover. The no-load, RSS and paired-delta protocols are all substantive now, and the unit deferral is correctly scoped, since exclusion membership, inventory completeness, layer cardinality and the millisecond bounds all stay scored. The objection is one mechanism. noLoadProtocol specifies 'strace -f … of the timed child T' on Linux, and strace is ptrace-based, while D-102's preflight paragraph says observation is a dedicated launch that is never a timing sample and that timing samples proceed without ptrace or suspend. G03's job record carries the latencies and the event stream together, so as written the traced launch is the timed one, in an artifact whose own protocol field says it does not amend D-102. Executed literally it either breaks D-102 or measures G03's latencies under strace against millisecond bounds that are scored now. macOS is unaffected, since fs_usage is kdebug-based and the sandbox alternative is a denial policy. I graded it SHOULD-FIX because nothing false is asserted about D-102 and a charitable author could run a separate launch, and I note Codex may reasonably grade it a blocker. The repair is narrow and D-102 already models it: make the observed launch a dedicated one that is never a timing sample.
